name: Naga Ghost Chili Chutney (Raja Mircha Chutney)
instructions: 1. Roast the fresh King Chilies and tomatoes over an open flame until the skins are charred and blackened. 2. Peel the charred skins from the tomatoes. 3. In a mortar and pestle, crush the garlic cloves and salt into a coarse paste. 4. Add the charred King Chilies and mash them carefully (ensure you wear gloves). 5. Add the charred tomatoes and the fermented soybean (Axone) and mash until combined. 6. Fold in the chopped onions and garnish with fresh coriander before serving.
description: Naga Ghost Chili Chutney is a quintessential accompaniment in Naga cuisine, known for its intense heat and smoky flavor profile. It reflects the Naga people's love for bold flavors and their reliance on locally sourced ingredients like the world-renowned King Chili and fermented soybean (Axone), serving as a staple side dish to balance simple steamed rice and boiled vegetables.
